evidence.quote: The alloy used in the present study was a commercial Mg–3 mass% Al–1 mass% Zn alloy, AZ31.

evidence.quote: The test revealed that the m-value at a nominal strain of 75% was 0.49.
This high m-value of 0.5 suggests that grain boundary sliding could be a dominant deformation process [17].
the m-value reduced to a small value, indicating that dislocation creep dominated deformation [17].
It is obvious that the grain boundary sliding, which is the principal mode of deformation in Region II, brought about texture weakening.

The texture strengthening ought to be caused by basal slip, especially in the early stage of deformation, because basal slip is the most active slip system in AZ31 alloy even at elevated temperatures[26].
This is readily explained from the fact that plasticity controlled cavity growth is the dominant mechanism during superplastic ﬂow in magnesium-based materials[20–22].
The lower strength and higher elongation of the specimens deformed in Region II are associated with the fact that much grains are now favorably oriented for basal slip.
